classification.difficultyReason: The parts scaffold the triangle and sine-rule equation; expand the difference, isolate a tangent value and recognise it exactly using a familiar angle difference.

spec.description: Unshaded wide triangle with horizontal base AB, C above and nearer A, AC labelled 3, AB labelled 3 + 3√3, angle A labelled 30° and angle B labelled θ.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(3+3√3,0), C=(3 cos 30°,3 sin 30°). These coordinates use the supplied side lengths and angle. All three edges are solid. Coordinate-derived angle sectors retain the supplied labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the value of θ and the angle at C are not supplied.

children.prompt: Point $B$ is chosen so that $AB$ has length $3+3\sqrt{3}$ and $\angle ABC=\theta$, where $0<\theta<90^\circ$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the size of $\angle ACB$ in terms of $\theta$.

answer.worked:
The angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-30^\circ-\theta\\\angle ACB&=150^\circ-\theta.\end{align*}$$

Using the sine-difference expansion in part (b),
$$\begin{align*}\sin150^\circ\cos\theta-\cos150^\circ\sin\theta&=(1+\sqrt{3})\sin\theta\\\frac12\cos\theta+\frac{\sqrt{3}}2\sin\theta&=(1+\sqrt{3})\sin\theta\\\cos\theta&=(2+\sqrt{3})\sin\theta\\\tan\theta&=\frac{1}{2+\sqrt{3}}\\\tan\theta&=2-\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$$
Also,
$$\begin{align*}\tan15^\circ&=\tan(45^\circ-30^\circ)\\\tan15^\circ&=\frac{1-1/\sqrt{3}}{1+1/\sqrt{3}}\\\tan15^\circ&=2-\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$$
Since $0<\theta<90^\circ$, $\theta=15^\circ$.
